πρίν.as:
πρίν,
1. as adv. of time, before, formerly (cl.; III Mac 5:286:4, 31).
2. As conjc. (cl.), before;
(a) after a positive sentence, c. acc. et inf.: Mt 26:34, 75, Mk 14:72, Lk 22:61, Jo 4:498:58 (where D. om. γενέσθαι and π. becomes prep. c. gen.; v. Bl., § 69, 7) 14:29, Ac 2:20(LXX), WH, txt.; πρὶν ἤ (not such good Attic in this construction; v. Bl., § 69, 7), Mt 1:18, Mk 14:30, Ac 2:20, WH, mg., 7:2;
(b) after a negative sentence, πρὶν ἤ: a. subjc. (seq. ἄν, M, Pr., 169), Lk 2:26; c. optat., Ac 25:16.†

προφήτης.long: a prophet, poet; a person gifted at expositing divine truth.
προφήτης.sd: a foreteller ("prophet"); by analogy, an inspired speaker; by extension, a poet
προφήτης.der: from a compound of G4253 (πρό) and G5346 (φημί);
προφήτης.as:
προφήτης, -ου, ὁ [< πρόφημι, to speak forth),
[in LXX chiefly for נָבִיא;]
one who acts as an interpreter or forth-teller of the Divine will (v. Lft., Notes, 83 f.; Tr., Syn., § vi), a prophet;
1. in cl. (Æsch., Hdt., Plat., al.), of the interpreters of oracles.
2. In NT,
(a) of the OT prophets: Mt 5:12, Mk 6:15, Lk 4:27, Jo 8:52, Ro 11:3, al.;
(b) of prophets in general: Mt 10:4113:5721:46, Mk 6:4, Lk 13:33, al.;
(c) of John the Baptist: Mt 21:26, Mk 6:15, Lk 1:76;
(d) of Christ: Mt 21:11, Jo 6:14, Ac 3:22, 237:37 (LXX);
(e) of Christian prophets in the apostolic age: Ac 15:32, I Co 12:28, Eph 2:20, al.;
(f) by meton., of the writings of prophets: Lk 24:27, Ac 8:28, al.;
(g) of a poet: Tit 1:12 (on the use of the term in π. and Inscr., v. Deiss., BS, 235 f.; MM, xxii).

προστάσσω.long: (a) I instruct, command, (b) I appoint, assign.
προστάσσω.as:
προσ-τάσσω,
[in LXX chiefly for צוה pi.;]
1. c. acc. pers., to place at, to attach to.
2.to give a command, enjoin, appoint: Lk 5:14; c. dat. pers., Mt 1:24; c. acc. rei, Mt 8:4, Mk 1:44; c. acc. et inf., Ac 10:48; pass., Ac 10:3317:26.†

προσκυνέω.long: I go down on my knees to, do obeisance to, worship.
προσκυνέω.sd: to fawn or crouch to, i.e. (literally or figuratively) prostrate oneself in homage (do reverence to, adore)
προσκυνέω.der: from G4314 (πρός) and a probable derivative of G2965 (κύων) (meaning to kiss, like a dog licking his master's hand);
προσκυνέω.as:
προσ-κυνέω, -ῶ
(< κυνέω, to kiss), [in LXX chiefly for שׁחה hith.;]
to make obeisance, do reverence to, worship;
(a) prop. (as in cl., of the gods: Hdt., Æsch., Plat., al.), of God, Christ and supra-mundane beings: absol., Jo 4:2012:20, Ac 8:2724:11, He 11:21 (Westc., in l.), Re 11:1; πίπτειν καὶ π., Re 5:14; c. dat. (of the significance of this constr. as compared with the usual cl., c. acc., v. Abbott, JG, 78 f.; JV, 133 ff.), Jo 4:21, 23, Ac 7:43, I Co 14:25, He 1:6, Re 4:107:1111:1613:4, 1514:716:219:4, 10, 2022:8, 9; c. acc. (v. supr.), Mt 4:10, Lk 4:824:52 (WH, R, mg., om.), Jo 4:22, 24, Re 9:2013:4, 8, 1214:9, 1120:4; seq. ἐπώπιον, Lk 4:7, Re 15:4;
(b) as in cl., of homage to human superiors (cf. MM, xxi): absol., Mt 20:20, Ac 10:25; c. dat. (v. supr.), Mt 2:2, 88:29:1814:3315:2518:2628:9, Mk 15:19, Jo 9:38; πεσὼν π., Mt 2:114:9; ἐνώπιον τ. ποδῶν, Re 3:9; c. acc., Mk 5:6 (dat. T).†

προάγω.long: (a) trans: I lead forth; in the judicial sense, into court, (b) intrans. and trans: I precede, go before, (c) intrans: I go too far.
προάγω.sd: to lead forward (magisterially); intransitively, to precede (in place or time (participle, previous))
προάγω.as:
προ-άγω,
[in LXX: I Ki 17:16 (נגשׁ), Wi 19:11, al.;]
1. prop. trans., to lead on, lead forth or forward: c. acc. pers., Ac 16:3017:5; of bringing forth to trial, Ac 12:6 (WH, txt., προσάγ-); seq. ἐπί, c. gen. pers., Ac 25:26.
2. Intrans. (Plat., Polyb., and later writers; v. Bl., § 53, 1; MM, xxi);
(a)to lead the way, I Ti 1:18 (R, mg.), hence, to go before, precede: Lk 18:39; opp. to ἀκολουθέω, Mk 11:9; seq. εἰς, Mt 14:22, Mk 6:45, I Ti 5:24, He 7:18; c. acc. pers., Mt 2:921:9, Mk 10:32; seq. εἰς, Mt 21:3126:3228:7, Mk 14:2816:7;
(b)to go on, advance (Si 20:27): II Jo 9.†

προσφέρω.long: (a) I bring to, (b) characteristically: I offer (of gifts, sacrifices, etc).
προσφέρω.sd: to bear towards, i.e. lead to, tender (especially to God), treat
προσφέρω.kj: bring (to, unto), deal with, do, offer (unto, up), present unto, put to
προσφέρω.der: from G4314 (πρός) and G5342 (φέρω) (including its alternate);
προσφέρω.as:
προσ-φέρω,
[in LXX chiefly for קרב hi.;]
1.to bring to, lead to: c. acc. et dat. pers., Mt 4:248:169:2, 3214:3517:16, Mk 2:4 (WH, R, txt.; sc. αὐτόν) 10:13, Lk 18:1523:14; pass., Mt 12:22 (act., WH, txt.) 18:24 (προσήχθη, WH) 19:13; c. acc. rei, Mt 25:20; id. c. dat. pers., Mt 22:19, Lk 23:36; τ. στόματι, Jo 19:29; metaph., c. dat pers., to deal with, He 12:7 (cl.).
2.to offer: Mt 2:11, Ac 8:18; esp. (as freq. in LXX; cf. FlJ, Ant., iii, 9, 3) sacrifices, gifts and prayers to God: absol., seq. περί (ὑπέρ), Mk 1:44, Lk 5:14, He 5:1, 39:710:12; pass., Ac 21:26; c. acc. rei (δῶρον, θυσίαν, λυτρείαν, προσφοράν), Mt 5:23, 24 (aoristic pres.; M, Pr., 247) 8:4, Jo 16:2, Ac 7:4221:26, He 5:18:3, 49:7, 910:1, 2, 8, 11, 12; δεήσεις τε κ. ἱκετηρίας, He 5:7; c. acc. pers., He 11:17 (conative impf.; M, Pr., 129); of Christ, He 7:27 (ἀνενέγκας, WH, txt.) 9:14, 25, 28.†

πρός.sd: a preposition of direction; forward to, i.e. toward (with the genitive case, the side of, i.e. pertaining to; with the dative case, by the side of, i.e. near to; usually with the accusative case, the place, time, occasion, or respect, which is the destination of the relation, i.e. whither or for which it is predicated)
πρός.kj: about, according to , against, among, at, because of, before, between, (where-)by, for, X at thy house, in, for intent, nigh unto, of, which pertain to, that, to (the end that), X together, to (you) -ward, unto, with(-in)
πρός.as:
πρός,
prep. c. gen., dat., acc.
I. C. gen., of motion from a place, from the side of, hence metaph., in the interests of, Ac 27:34 (cf. Page, in l.).
II. C. dat., of local proximity, hard by, near, at: Mk 5:11, Lk 19:37, Jo 18:1620:11, 12, Re 1:13.
III. C. acc., of motion or direction towards a place or object, to, towards.
1. Of place,
(a) after verbs of motion or of speaking and other words with the idea of direction: ἔρχομαι, ἀναβαίνω, πορεύομαι, λέγω, ἐπιστολή, etc., Mt 3:14, Mk 6:51, Lk 11:5, Jo 2:3, Ac 9:2, al. mult.; metaph., of mental direction, hostile or otherwise, Lk 23:12, Jo 6:52, II Co 7:4, Eph 6:12, Col 3:13, al.; of the issue or end, Lk 14:32, Jo 11:4, al.; of purpose, Mt 26:12, Ro 3:26, I Co 6:5, al.; πρὸς τό, c. inf., denoting purpose (cf. M, Pr., 218, 220; Lft., Notes, 131), Mt 5:28, Mk 13:22, Eph 6:11, I Th 2:9, al.;
(b) of close proximity, at, by, with: Mt 3:10, Mk 11:4, Lk 4:11, Ac 3:2, al.; after εἶναι, Mt 13:56, Mk 6:3, Jo 1:1, al.
2. Of time,
(a)towards (Plat., Xen., LXX: Ge 8:11, al.): Lk 24:29;
(b)for: πρὸς καιρόν, Lk 8:13, I Co 7:5; πρὸς ὥραν, Jo 5:35, al.; πρὸς ὀλίγον, Ja 4:14.
3. Of relation
(a)toward, with: Ro 5:1, II Co 1:12, Col 4:5, I Th 4:12, al.;
(b)with regard to: Mt 19:8, Mk 12:12, Ro 8:31, al.;
(c)pertaining to, to: Mt 27:4, Jo 21:22, Ro 15:17, He 2:175:1;
(d)according to: Lk 12:47, II Co 5:10, Ga 2:14, Eph 3:44:14;
(e)in comparison with: Ro 8:18.
IV. In composition: towards (προσέρχομαι), to (προσάγω), against (προσκόπτω), besides (προσδαπανάω).

πρέπω.long: it becomes, is fitting to, is right.
πρέπω.sd: to tower up (be conspicuous), i.e. (by implication) to be suitable or proper (third person singular present indicative, often used impersonally, it is fit or right)
πρέπω.as:
πρέπω,
[in LXX: Ps 92 (93):5 (נאה pi.), etc.;]
1.to be clearly seen.
2.to resemble.
3.to be fitting or becoming, to suit: c. dat., He 7:26, I Ti 2:10, Tit 2:1; impers., c. dat., Eph 5:3; id. seq. inf., He 2:10; πρέπον ἐστίν, c. dat. pers. et inf., Mt 3:15; c. acc. et inf., I Co 11:13 (v. Bl., § 72, 5).†

προσέρχομαι.long: I come up to, come to, come near (to), approach, consent (to).
προσέρχομαι.sd: to approach, i.e. (literally) come near, visit, or (figuratively) worship, assent to
προσέρχομαι.kj: (as soon as he) come (unto), come thereunto, consent, draw near, go (near, to, unto)
προσέρχομαι.der: from G4314 (πρός) and G2064 (ἔρχομαι) (including its alternate);
προσέρχομαι.as:
προσ-έρχομαι,
[in LXX for קרב, נגשׁ, etc.;]
to approach, draw near: absol., Mt 4:11, Lk 9:42, al.; c. infin., Mt 24:1, al.; c. dat. loc., He 12:18, 22; dat. pers., Mt 5:1, and freq., Jo 12:21, al.; ptcp., προσελθών, c. indic., Mt 8:2, and freq., Mk 1:31, Lk 7:14, al.; π. αὐτῷ, c. indic., Mt 4:3, Mk 6:35. Metaph.,
(a) of approaching God: absol. (Le 21:17, De 21:5, al.), He 10:1, 22; τ. θεῷ, He 7:2511:6; τ. θρόνῳ τ. χάριτος, He 4:16; πρὸς Χριστόν, I Pe 2:4;
(b) in sense not found elsewhere (Field, Notes, 211), to consent to: ὑγιαίνουσι λόγοις, I Ti 6:3.

προσκόπτω.long: I stumble, strike the foot against, beat upon, take offense at.
προσκόπτω.sd: to strike at, i.e. surge against (as water); specially, to stub on, i.e. trip up (literally or figuratively)
προσκόπτω.as:
προσ-κόπτω,
[in LXX for נגף, כּשׁל ni., etc.;]
1. trans., to strike (e.g. hand or foot) against: c. acc. seq. πρός, fig., Mt 4:6, Lk 4:11(LXX).
2. Intrans., to stumble: absol. (To 11:9, Pr 3:23), Jo 11:9, 10; of wind, to rush against, beat upon: c. dat, Mt 7:27. Metaph., in late writers,
(a)to offend (Polyb.);
(b)to take offence at, stumble at: seq. ἐν, Ro 14:21; c. dat., τ. λόγῳ, I Pe 2:8; τ. λίθῳ τ. προσκόμματος, Ro 9:32.†

προβαίνω.sd: to walk forward, i.e. advance (literally, or in years)
προβαίνω.kj: + be of a great age, go farther (on), be well stricken
προβαίνω.der: from G4253 (πρό) and the base of G939 (βάσις);
προβαίνω.as:
προ-βαίνω,
[in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא;]
to go forwards, go on, advance: Mt 4:21, Mk 1:19. Metaph., of age (Ge 18:11, al., Lys., Diod., al.), ἐν τ. ἡμέραις, Lk 1:7, 182:36.†

πραΰς.as:
πραΰς, -εῖα, -ΰ, and πρᾷος
(or πρᾶος, v. Bl., § 3, 3), -α, -ον (v. LS, Thayer, s.v.), [in LXX (always -ΰς, exc. II Mac 15:12, -ᾷος, v. Thackeray, Gr., 180 f.) for עָנָו, עָנָיו, עָנִי;]
gentle, meek: Mt 5:511:2921:5(LXX), I Pe 3:4.†

πρό.long: (a) of place: before, in front of, (b) of time: before, earlier than.
πρό.sd: "fore", i.e. in front of, prior (figuratively, superior) to
πρό.as:
πρό,
prep. c. gen.,
[in LXX chiefly for לִפְנֵי;]
before;
(a) of place: Ac 12:6, 1414:13, Ja 5:9; π. προσώπου (= Heb. לִפְנֵי, De 3:18, Ma 3:1, al.; Bl., § 40, 9), Mt 11:10, Mk 1:2, Lk 1:767:279:5210:1, Ac 14:13;
(b) of time: Mt 8:2924:38, Lk 11:3821:12, Jo 11:5513:117:24, Ac 5:3621:38, I Co 2:74:5, Eph 1:4, Col 1:17, II Ti 1:94:21, Tit 1:2, He 11:5, I Pe 1:20, Ju 25; π. ἐτῶν δεκατεσσάρων, fourteen years ago, II Co 12:2; π. προσώπου (v. supr.), Ac 13:24; c. gen. pers., Mt 5:12, Jo 5:710:8, Ro 16:7, Ga 1:17; c. gen. art. inf. (= πρίν; M, Pr., 100; Bl., § 69, 7), Mt 6:8, Lk 2:2122:15, Jo 1:4913:1917:5, Ac 23:15, Ga 2:123:23; as in late writers (resembling a Latin idiom but independent of it; B1., § 40, 5; M, Pr., 100 f.; cf. Am 1:1, II Mac 15:36, and for other exx., Soph., Lex., s.v.), πρὸ ἓξ ἡμέρας τοῦ πασχα, on the sixth day bef. the Passover, Jo 12:1;
(c) of preference: π. πάντων, Ja 5:12, I Pe 4:8;
(d) in compos.,
α c. subst., of position before: προαύλιον, πρόδρομος; priority of rank or order, προπάτωρ; anticipation, πρόγνωσις, πρόνοια;
β c. adj., intensity, πρόδηλος;
γ c. verb., of place, προάγω, προβαίνω; of preference, προαιρέομαι.†

πρῶτος.sd: foremost (in time, place, order or importance)
πρῶτος.kj: before, beginning, best, chief(-est), first (of all), former
πρῶτος.as:
B. Superl., πρῶτος, -η, -ον,
[in LXX chiefly for רִאשׁוֹן, also for אֶחַד, etc.;]
first,
1. of Time or Place;
(a) absol., as subst., ὁ π.., Lk 14:18, Jo 19:32, I Co 14:30; ὁ π. καὶ ὁ ἔσχατος, Re 1:172:822:13; neut., τὸ π., opp. to τ. δεύτερον, He 10:9; τὰ π., opp. to τ. ἔσχατα, Mt 12:45, Lk 11:26, II Pe 2:20; anarth., Mt 10:2; pl., Mt 19:30, Mk 10:31, Lk 13:30; ἐν πρώτοις (EV, first of all), I Co 15:3;
(b) as adj.: πρώτῃ (sc. ἡμέρᾳ) σαββάτου, Mk 16:[9]; φυλακή, opp. to δευτέρα, Ac 12:10; equiv. to adv. in English, Jo 8:[7]20:4, 8, Ac 27:43, Ro 10:19, I Ti 1:16, I Jo 4:19; = πρότερος (v. infr.; cf. M, Pr., 79; Bl., § 11, 5; Thackeray, Gr., 183 f.): c. gen., π. μου ἦν (my chief: Abbott, Jg., 509 ff.; but cf. M, Pr., 245), Jo 1:15, 30; c. art., Mk 14:12, Ac 1:1, al.; seq. ὁ δεύτερος, etc., Mt 22:25, Mk 12:20, al.
2. Of Rank or Dignity, chief, principal: Mt 20:2722:38, Mk 9:35, Eph 6:2, al.; c. gen., Mk 12:28, 29 al.; πόλις (Field, Notes, 124), Ac 16:12; c. art., Lk 15:2219:47, Ac 13:50, al.
3. Neut., πρῶτον, as adv., first, at the first;
(a) of Time: Mt 8:21, Mk 4:28, al.; τὸ π., Jo 10:40, al.;
(b) of Order: Ro 3:2, I Co 11:18, al.

προσεύχομαι.long: I pray, pray for, offer prayer.
προσεύχομαι.sd: to pray to God, i.e. supplicate, worship
προσεύχομαι.as:
προσ-εύχομαι,
[in LXX chiefly for פלל hith.;]
to pray (always of prayer to God, or in cl., to gods): absol., Mt 6:5-7, 914:2319:1326:36, 39, 41, 44, Mk 1:356:4611:24, 2513:33 (WH, R, txt., om.) Mk 14:32, 38, 39, Lk 1:103:215:166:129:18, 28, 2911:1, 218:1, 1022:44 (WH, R, mg., om.), Ac 1:246:69:11, 4010:9, 3011:512:1213:314:2316:2520:3621:522:1728:8, I Co 11:4, 514:14, I Th 5:17, I Ti 2:8, Ja 5:13, 18; seq. λέγων, Mt 26:39, 42, Lk 22:41; c. dat. instr., I Co 11:514:14, 15; μακρά, Mt 23:14 (WH, R, txt., om.), Mk 12:40, Lk 20:47; ἐν πνεύματι (ἁγίῳ), Eph 6:18, Ju 20; προσευχῇ π. (a Hebraism, v.s. προσευχή), Ja 5:17; c. acc. rei, Lk 18:11, Ro 8:26; seq. ἐπί, c. acc. pers., Ja 5:14; c. dat. pers., Mt 6:6, I Co 11:13; seq. περί, c. gen., Ac 8:15, Col 1:34:3, I Th 5:25, II Th 1:113:1, He 13:18; ὑπέρ, Mt 5:44, Lk 6:28, Col 1:9, Ja 5:16; seq. ἵνα, Mt 24:20, Mk 13:1814:35, Lk 22:46, I Co 14:13; τοῦτο ἵνα, Phl 1:9; c. inf., Lk 22:46; seq. τοῦ, c. inf. (Bl., § 71, 3), Ja 5:17.†

προσέχω.g: I pay attention to, devote myself to
προσέχω.long: (a) I attend to, pay attention to, (b) I beware, am cautious, (c) I join, devote myself to.
προσέχω.sd: (figuratively) to hold the mind (3563 implied) towards, i.e. pay attention to, be cautious about, apply oneself to, adhere to
προσέχω.kj: (give) attend(-ance, -ance at, -ance to, unto), beware, be given to, give (take) heed (to unto); have regard
προσέχω.as:
προσ-έχω,
[in LXX for קשׁב hi., שׁמר ni., etc.;]
1.to turn to, bring to (freq. ναῦν, expressed or understood, to bring to port, land; Hdt., al.).
2.τ. νοῦν, seq. dat., to turn one's mind to, attend to; in Xen. and later writers with νοῦν omitted (Bl., § 53, 1; 81, 1): Ac 8:616:14, He 2:1, II Pe 1:19; in sense of caring or providing for, Ac 20:28; π. ἑαυτῷ, to give heed to oneself (M, Pr., 157; cf. Ge 24:6, Ex 10:28, al.): Lk 17:321:34, Ac 5:35; id. seq. ἀπό (M, Pr., 102; Bl., § 34, 11; 40, 3; v.s. βλέπω), Lk 12:1; (without dat.) Mt 7:1510:1716:6, 11, 12, Lk 20:46 (cf. Si 6:13, al.); seq. μή, c. inf. (M, Pr., 193; Bl., § 69, 4), Mt 6:1.
3.to attach or devote oneself to: c. dat. pers., Ac 8:10, 11, I Ti 4:1; c. dat. rei, I Ti 1:43:84:136:3 T (-ερχ-, WH, R), Tit 1:14, He 7:13.†

πρόσωπον.sd: the front (as being towards view), i.e. the countenance, aspect, appearance, surface; by implication, presence, person
πρόσωπον.kj: (outward) appearance, X before, countenance, face, fashion, (men's) person, presence
πρόσωπον.der: from G4314 (πρός) and (the visage, from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι));
πρόσωπον.as:
πρόσωπον, -ου, τό
(< πρός, ὤψ), [in LXX chiefly and very freq. for פָּנִים;]
1. prop., of persons (so always in cl.);
(a)the face, countenance: Mt 6:16, 17, Mk 14:65, Lk 9:29, II Co 3:7, Re 4:7, al.; τὸ π. τῆς γενέσεως (EV, natural face), Ja 1:23; πίπτειν ἐπὶ (τὰ) π., Mt 17:6, Lk 5:12, Re 7:11, al.; ἀγνοούμενος τῷ π., Ga 1:22; π., οὐ καρδίᾳ, I Th 2:17; κατὰ πρόσωπον (in front, facing: Thuc., Xen., al.), when present, face to face, Ac 25:16, II Co 10:1, 7, Ga 2:11; id. c. gen., as compound prep., in the presence of (not cl.; v. Bl., § 40, 9; M, Pr., 99 f.; Thackeray, Gr., 43 f.), Lk 2:31, Ac 3:13; similarly ἀπὸ π. (Heb. מִלִּפְּנֵי; v. Dalman, Words, 29), from the presence of, Ac 3:195:417:45, II Th 1:9, Re 12:1420:11; πρὸ π. (Heb. לִפְנֵי), before, Mt 11:10, Mk 1:2, Lk 7:27(LXX), al.; in other phrases resembling Heb. idiom (Thackeray, Gr., 42), βλέπειν (ὁρᾶν, θεωρεῖν, ἰδεῖν) τὸ π., to see one's face, i.e. see him in person, Mt 18:10, Ac 20:25, 38, I Th 3:10, Re 22:4; ἐμφανισθῆναι τῷ π. τοῦ θεοῦ, He 9:24; ἐν π. Χριστοῦ, II Co 2:104:6; μετὰ τοῦ π. σου, with thy presence, Ac 2:28(LXX); εἰς π. τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν, II Co 8:24; στηρίζειν τὸ π. (Heb. שׂוּםפָּנִים: Je 21:10, al.; v. Dalman, Words, 30), c. inf., to set one's face towards, Lk 9:51; similarly, τὸ π. αὐτοῦ ἦν πορευόμενον (op. cit., 31), Lk 9:53; τὸ π. τοῦ κυρίου ἐπί, I Pe 3:12(LXX);
(b)form, person: καυχᾶσθαι ἐν π. καὶ μὴ ἐν καρδίᾳ, II Co 5:12 (cf. I Ki 16:7); metaph., as in Heb. idiom, of judgment according to appearance, external condition or circumstances (נשָׂאָprobably misspelled נָשָׂאפָּנִים; v. Dalman, Words, 30; Thackeray, Gr., 43 f.): λαμβάνειν π., Lk 20:21, Ga 2:6; βλέπειν εἰς π., Mt 22:16, Mk 12:14; θαυμάζειν πρόσωπα, Ju 16.
2. Of things (cf. Dalman, Words, 30);
(a)face, appearance (Ps 103 (104):30): Mt 16:3 (WH, R, mg., om.), Lk 12:56, Ja 1:11;
(b)surface (Ge 2:6): Lk 21:35, Ac 17:26.

προστίθημι.g: I put to, add, do again
προστίθημι.long: I place (put) to, add; I do again.
προστίθημι.sd: to place additionally, i.e. lay beside, annex, repeat
προστίθημι.kj: add, again, give more, increase, lay unto, proceed further, speak to any more
προστίθημι.as:
προσ-τίθημι,
[in LXX chiefly for יסף hi., also for אסף ni., etc.;]
1.to put to.
2.to add, join to, give in addition: c. acc. seq. ἐπί, Mt 6:27, Lk 3:2012:25; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, Ac 2:47; c. acc. et dat., Lk 17:5, He 12:19 (v. MM, xxi); pass., absol., Ac 2:41, Ga 3:19; c. dat., Mt 6:33, Mk 4:24, Lk 12:31, Ac 5:1411:24; προσετέθη πρὸς τ. πατέρας (cf. Ge 26:8, Jg 2:10, al.), Ac 13:36; c. inf., of repeating or continuing the action signified by the following verb, as in Heb. idiom (Ge 4:28:12, al.; cf. WM, § 54, 5; Lft. on Clem., I Co., xii; but v. also M, Pr., 67, 233; Deiss., BS, 671; MM, xxi), Lk 20:11, Ac 12:3; similarly ptcp., προσθείς, c. indic. (Ge 38:5, al.), Lk 19:11.†

πρόβατον.sd: something that walks forward (a quadruped), i.e. (specially), a sheep (literally or figuratively)
πρόβατον.der: probably neuter of a presumed derivative of G4260 (προβαίνω);
πρόβατον.as:
πρόβατον, -ου, τό
(< προβαίνω), [in LXX chiefly for צֹאן, also for שֶׂה, more rarely for כֶּבֶשׂ (כֶּשֶׂב), רָחֵל;]
1. in Hom., Hdt., cattle, esp. of small cattle, sheep and goats.
2. In NT, as in Attic writers generally (cf. MM, xxi), a sheep: Mt 7:15, Mk 6:34, al.; πρόβατα σφαγῆς, Ro 8:36(LXX). Metaph. (in cl. of timidity, stupidity or idleness), of the followers of a leader or master, esp. of those who are subject to the care of the Good Shepherd: Mt 10:615:2426:31(LXX), Mk 14:27(LXX), Jo 10:7, 8, 15, 16, 26, 2721:16, 17 (WH txt., προβάτια), He 13:20; opp. to ἐρίφια, Mt 25:33.

προφητεύω.long: I foretell, prophesy; I set forth matter of divine teaching by special faculty.
προφητεύω.sd: to foretell events, divine, speak under inspiration, exercise the prophetic office
προφητεύω.as:
προφητεύω
(< προφήτης), [in LXX chiefly for נבא ni., hith.;]
to be aπροφήτης (q.v.), to prophesy: in the primary sense of telling forth the Divine counsels, Mt 7:2226:68, Mk 14:65, Lk 1:6722:64, Ac 19:6, I Co 11:4, 513:914:1, 3-5, 24, 31, 39, Re 11:3; with the idea of foretelling future events (an idea merely incidental, not essential; v. Lft., Notes, 83 f.), Mt 11:13, Ac 2:17, 18(LXX)21:9; seq. περί, Mt 15:7, Mk 7:6, I Pe 1:10; ἐπί, c. dat., Re 10:11; λέγων, Ju 14; ὅτι, Jo 11:51.†
SYN.: μαντεύομαι, q.v.

προσπίπτω.g: I fall down before, beat against
προσπίπτω.long: (a) I fall down before, (b) I beat against, rush violently upon.
προσπίπτω.sd: to fall towards, i.e. (gently) prostrate oneself (in supplication or homage), or (violently) to rush upon (in storm)
προσπίπτω.as:
προσ-πίπτω,
[in LXX for נפל, נגע hi., כּרע;]
1.to fall upon, strike against: c. dat., of wind, Mt 7:25.
2.to fall down at one's feet, fall prostrate before: absol., seq. πρός, Mk 7:25; c. dat. pers., Mk 3:115:33, Lk 8:28, 47, Ac 16:29; τ. γόνασιν, Lk 5:8.†

προσκαλέομαι.sd: to call toward oneself, i.e. summon, invite
προσκαλέομαι.der: middle voice from G4314 (πρός) and G2564 (καλέω);
προσκαλέομαι.as:
προσ-καλέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX chiefly for קרא;]
to call to. Mid., to call to oneself (v. M, Pr., 157): c. acc. pers., Mt 10:1, Mk 3:136:7, Lk 7:19, Ac 5:40, Ja 5:14, al. Metaph., of the Divine call: Ac 2:39; c. inf., Ac 16:10 (v. Bl., § 69, 4); seq. εἰς, Ac 13:2.†

προσδοκάω.long: I expect, wait for, await, think, anticipate.
προσδοκάω.sd: to anticipate (in thought, hope or fear); by implication, to await
προσδοκάω.kj: (be in) expect(-ation), look (for), when looked, tarry, wait for
προσδοκάω.as:
προσ-δοκάω, -ῶ
(the simple verb exists only in the forms δοκέω, -εύω), [in LXX: Ps 103 (104):27 (שׂבר pi.), etc.;]
to await, expect: Mt 24:50, Lk 3:1512:46, Ac 27:3328:6; c. acc. pers., Mt 11:3, Lk 1:217:19, 208:40, Ac 10:24; c. acc. rei, II Pe 3:12-14; c. acc. et inf., Ac 28:6; c. inf., Ac 3:5.†

προσφωνέω.long: I call to, summon; I call (out) to, address, give a speech to, harangue.
προσφωνέω.sd: to sound towards, i.e. address, exclaim, summon
προσφωνέω.as:
προσ-φωνέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: I Es 2:216:6, 22, II Mac 15:15*;]
1.to address, call to; in cl., c. acc. pers., c. dupl. acc. (cf. II Mac 15:15); absol. (Hom., Od., v, 159, al.): Ac 21:40. In late writers, c. dat. pers.: Mt 11:16, Lk 7:3213:1223:20, Ac 22:2.
2.to call by name, summon: c. acc. (as in cl.), Lk 6:13.†

πρόθεσις.long: a setting forth, the show-bread; predetermination, purpose.
πρόθεσις.sd: a setting forth, i.e. (figuratively) proposal (intention); specially, the show-bread (in the Temple) as exposed before God
πρόθεσις.as:
πρό-θεσις, -εως, ἡ,
[in LXX: Ex 40:4, 23 (עֵרֶךְ), I Ch 9:32, al. (מַעֲרֶכֶת), II Ch 4:19 (פָּנִים), I Mac 1:22, II Mac 3:8, al.;]
1.a setting forth (Plat., Plut., al.): οἱ ἄρτοι τῆς π. (cf. LXX, Ex 40:4, 23, I Ch 9:32, II Ch 4:19, I Mac 1:22, II Mac 3:8, elsewhere ἄρτοι ἐνώπιοι, Ex 25:29; οἱ ἄ. τοῦ προσώπου, Ne 10:33), Mt 12:4, Mk 2:26, Lk 6:4; ἡ π. τῶν ἄρτων, He 9:2.
2.a purpose (Mist., Polyb., al.; II Mac 3:8): Ac 11:2327:13, Ro 8:289:11, Eph 1:113:11, II Ti 1:93:10.†

προφητεία.long: prophecy, prophesying; the gift of communicating and enforcing revealed truth.
προφητεία.as:
† προφητεία, -ας, ἡ
(< προψητεύω), [in LXX for נְבוּאָה, חָזוֹן;]
the gift (and its exercise) of interpreting the Divine will and purpose, prophecy, prophesying: of OT prophecy, Mt 13:14, II Pe 1:20, 21; of NT prophecy, Ro 12:6, I Co 12:1013:214:6, 22, I Ti 4:14, Re 11:622:19; pl., I Co 13:8, I Th 5:20, I Ti 1:18; οἱ λόγοι τῆς π., Re 1:322:7, 10, 18; τ. πνεῦμα τῆς π., Re 19:10 (Luc., FlJ, LXX, π.; v. Deiss., BS, 235 f.; MM, xxii).†

πρόσκαιρος.sd: for the occasion only, i.e. temporary
πρόσκαιρος.kj: dur-(eth) for awhile, endure for a time, for a season, temporal
πρόσκαιρος.as:
** πρόσ-καιρος, -ον,
[in LXX: IV Mac 15:2, 8, 23*;]
1.in season.
2.for a season, temporary, transient: II Co 4:18, He 11:25; of plants, short-lived: Mt 13:21, Mk 4:17.†

προβιβάζω.long: I lead forward, lead on; met: I induce, incite, urge.
προβιβάζω.sd: to force forward, i.e. bring to the front, instigate
προβιβάζω.der: from G4253 (πρό) and a reduplicated form of G971 (βιάζω);
προβιβάζω.as:
προ-βιβάζω, causal of προβαίνω,
[in LXX: Ex 35:34 (ירה hi.), De 6:7 (שׁנן pi.)*;]
to lead forward, lead on; metaph., to induce, incite, urge: Mt 14:8.†

πρεσβύτερος.long: elder, usually used as subst.; an elder, a member of the Sanhedrin, an elder of a Christian assembly.
πρεσβύτερος.sd: older; as noun, a senior; specially, an Israelite Sanhedrist (also figuratively, member of the celestial council) or Christian "presbyter"

προσμένω.long: I remain; I abide in, remain in, persist in, adhere to.
προσμένω.sd: to stay further, i.e. remain in a place, with a person; figuratively, to adhere to, persevere in
προσμένω.kj: abide still, be with, cleave unto, continue in (with)
προσμένω.as:
προσ-μένω,
[in LXX: Jg 3:25 A (חוּל hi.), To 2:2א, Wi 3:9, III Mac 7:17*;]
1.to wait longer, continue, remain still: Ac 18:18; seq. ἐν, I Ti 1:3.
2. C. dat., to remain with: Mt 15:32, Mk 8:32. Metaph., to remain attached to, cleave unto, abide in: τ. κυρίῳ, Ac 11:23 (R, txt.; ἐν τ. κ., R, mg., v. supr.); τ. χάριτι τ. θεοῦ, Ac 13:43; τ. δεήσεσιν, I Ti 5:5.†

πρωΐ.g: early in the morning, at dawn
πρωΐ.long: early in the morning, at dawn.
πρωΐ.sd: at dawn; by implication, the day-break watch
πρωΐ.as:
πρωί (Rec. πρωΐ),
adv.
(< πρό), [in LXX chiefly for בֹּקֶר, בַּבֹּקֶר;]
in the morning, early: Mt 16:3 (R, txt.) 21:18, Mk 1:3511:2013:3515:116:[9], Jo 18:2820:1; λίαν π., Mk 16:2; ἅμα π., Mt 20:1; ἀπὸ π. (cf. ἀπὸ πρωΐθεν, Ex 18:13), Ac 28:23.†

προσλαμβάνομαι.long: (a) I take to myself, (b) I take aside, (c) I welcome.
προσλαμβάνομαι.sd: to take to oneself, i.e. use (food), lead (aside), admit (to friendship or hospitality)
προσλαμβάνομαι.as:
προσ-λαμβάνω,
[in LXX: Ps 117 (18):16 (משׁה hi.), Ps 72 (73):24 (לקח), etc.;]
1.to take in addition.
2.to take to oneself, take, receive; in NT always mid., -ομαι;
(a) of things: of food, c. acc., Ac 27:33; c. gen. part., Ac 27:36;
(b) of persons: c. acc., Mt 16:22, Mk 8:32 (v. Swete, in l.), Ac 17:518:2628:2, Ro 14:1, 315:7, Phm 17.†

πρᾶξις.long: (a) a doing, action, mode of action; plur: deeds, acts, (b) function, business.
πρᾶξις.sd: practice, i.e. (concretely) an act; by extension, a function
πρᾶξις.as:
πρᾶξις, -εως, ἡ
(< πράσσω), [in LXX: II Ch 13:2227:728:26 (דֶּרֶךְ), Jb 24:5 A (פֹּעַל), Pr 13:13, Wi 9:11, al.;]
1.a doing, deed, act: Mt 16:27; pl., π. ἀποσπτόλων, Ac, tit.; in late writers especially of wicked deeds or practices (freq. in Polyb.): Lk 23:51; p1., Ro 8:13, Col 3:9; with ref. to magic (v. BS, 3235), Ac 19:18.
2.an acting, action, business, function: Ro 12:4.†

προφθάνω.sd: to get an earlier start of, i.e. anticipate
προφθάνω.as:
προ-φθάνω,
[in LXX chiefly for קדם pi.;]
c. ptcp. (as in cl., but more freq. the simple φθάνω, q.v.), to anticipate: Mt 17:25.†

πρᾶγμα.long: a thing done, a deed, action; a matter, an affair.
πρᾶγμα.sd: a deed; by implication, an affair; by extension, an object (material)
πρᾶγμα.as:
πρᾶγμα, -τος, τό
(< πράσσω), [in LXX chiefly for דָּבָר;]
1. that which has been done, a deed, act: Lk 1:1, Ac 5:4, II Co 7:11, He 6:18.
2. That which is being done (like Lat. res), hence, a thing, matter, affair: Mt 18:19, Ro 16:2, I Th 4:6 (v. M, Th., in l.), He 10:111:1, Ja 3:16; in forensic sense (as freq. in π., v. Deiss., BS, 233), a law-suit: I Co 6:1.†

προσευχή.long: (a) prayer (to God), (b) a place for prayer (used by Jews, perhaps where there was no synagogue).
προσευχή.as:
† προσ-ευχή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< προσεύχομαι), [in LXX chiefly for תְּפִלָּה;]
1.prayer to God: Mt 17:21 (WH, R, txt., om.) 21:22, Mk 9:29, Lk 22:45, Ac 3:16:410:31, Ro 12:12, I Co 7:5, Col 4:2; pl., Ac 2:4210:4, Ro 1:10, Eph 1:16, Col 4:12, I Th 1:2, Phm 4, 22, I Pe 3:74:7, Re 5:88:3, 4; οἶκος προσευχῆς, Mt 21:13, Mk 11:17, Lk 19:46 (LXX); π. καὶ δέησις, Eph 6:18, Phl 4:6; pl., I Ti 2:15:5; ἡ π. τοῦ θεοῦ, prayer to God (cf. Wi 16:28), Lk 6:12; πρὸς τ. θεόν, seq. ὑπέρ, Ac 12:5; pl., Ro 15:30; Hebraistically (Bl., § 38, 3), προσευχῇ προσεύχεσθαι, Ja 5:17 (EV, prayed fervently).
2.a place of prayer: of a synagogue (III Mac 7:20, v.l.; v. Charles, APOT, i, 173; for other exx., v. Kennedy, Sources, 114); of a place in the open (FlJ, Ant., xiv, 10, 23), Ac 16:13, 16.†
SYN.: v.s. δέησις.

πρωτοκλισία.g: the chief place at a banquet
πρωτοκλισία.long: the chief place at a banquet or table.
πρωτοκλισία.sd: a reclining first (in the place of honor) at the dinner-bed, i.e. preeminence at meals
πρωτοκλισία.as:
*† πρωτο-κλισία, -ας, ἡ,
the chief place at table (v. Swete, Mk 12:39): Mt 23:6, Mk 12:39, Lk 14:7, 820:46.†

πρωτοκαθεδρία.sd: a sitting first (in the front row), i.e. preeminence in council
πρωτοκαθεδρία.as:
*† πρωτοκαθεδρία, -ας, ἡ
(< πρῶιος, καθέδρα),
the chief seat: Mt 23:6, Mk 12:39 (v. Swete, in l.), Lk 11:4320:46.†

προσήλυτος.long: (lit: that has come to), a proselyte, that is a non-Jew, who has been circumcised and has adopted the Jews' religion.
προσήλυτος.sd: an arriver from a foreign region, i.e. (specially), an acceder (convert) to Judaism ("proselyte")
προσήλυτος.as:
† προσήλυτος, -ον
(< προσελαύνω), [in LXX for גֵּר;]
1.one who has arrived, a stranger.
2. Of converts to Judaism, a proselyte (v. DB, s.v.): Mt 23:15, Ac 2:106:513:43.†

προλέγω.long: I tell (say) beforehand, forewarn, declare, tell plainly.
προλέγω.sd: to say beforehand, i.e. predict, forewarn
προλέγω.as:
προ-λέγω,
[in LXX: Is 41:26 (נגד hi.)*;]
1.to tell or say beforehand: II Co 13:2, Ga 5:21, I Th 3:4 (R, txt.; cf. προεῖπον, but v. infr.).
2.to declare, tell plainly: II Co 13:2, Ga 5:21, I Th 3:4 (R, mg.; v. MM, xxi, and cf. Is 41:26).†

προέρχομαι.long: I go forward, go on, advance; I go before, precede.
προέρχομαι.sd: to go onward, precede (in place or time)
προέρχομαι.kj: go before (farther, forward), outgo, pass on
προέρχομαι.der: from G4253 (πρό) and G2064 (ἔρχομαι) (including its alternate);
προέρχομαι.as:
προ-έρχομαι,
[in LXX: Ge 33:3, 14 R (עבר), Jth 2:19, Si 35 (32):10, al;]
1.to go forward, go on, advance: seq. μικρόν, Mt 26:39 and Mk 14:35 (WH, mg., προσελθών): ῥύμην μίαν (cf. Plat., Rep., i, 328e), Ac 12:10.
2. Of relative position, to go before, precede: c. gen. (cl.; Jth 2:19); c. acc. pers. (not cl.), Lk 22:47 (c. gen., Rec.); seq. ἐνώπιον, Lk 1:17 (cf. Ge 33:3).
3. Of time, to go before or in advance: Ac 20:5, 13 (WH, mg., R, mg.), II Co 9:5; c. acc. pers. (= cl. φθάνω), Mk 6:33.†

πρόθυμος.sd: forward in spirit, i.e. predisposed; neuter (as noun) alacrity
πρόθυμος.as:
πρόθυμος, -ον,
[in LXX: I Ch 28:21, II Ch 29:31 (נָדִיב), Hb 1:8 (חוּשׁ), al.;]
willing, ready: Mt 26:41, Mk 14:38; neut., τὸ π. = ἡ προθυμία (Thuc., al., III Mac 5:26), οὕτως τὸ κατ’ ἐμὲ (= cl. τὸ ἐμὸν) π., Ro 1:15 (but v. ICC, in l.).†

πρωΐα.der: feminine of a derivative of G4404 (πρωΐ) as noun;

πραιτώριον.g: the official residence of the procurator
πραιτώριον.long: the palace at Jerusalem occupied by the Roman governor, or the quarters of the praetorian guard in Rome.
πραιτώριον.sd: the prætorium or governor's courtroom (sometimes including the whole edifice and camp)
πραιτώριον.as:
*† πραιτώριον, -ου, τό, (Lat. prætorium),
1.headquarters in a Roman camp.
2. The palace or official residence of the Governor of a province: Mt 27:27, Mk 15:16 (v. Swete, in l.), Jo 18:28, 3319:9; τ. π. τ. Ἡρῴδου, Ac 23:35.
3.the Prætorian Guard: Phl 1:13 (v. Lft., in l.; ICC, 51 f.).†

προσκυλίω.long: I roll to, roll up against.
προσκυλίω.sd: to roll towards, i.e. block against
προσκυλίω.as:
* προσ-κυλίω,
to roll up, roll to: c. acc. et dat., Mt 27:60; acc. seq. ἐπί, Mk 15:46.†

προσκαρτερέω.long: I persist, persevere in, continue steadfast in; I wait upon.
προσκαρτερέω.sd: to be earnest towards, i.e. (to a thing) to persevere, be constantly diligent, or (in a place) to attend assiduously all the exercises, or (to a person) to adhere closely to (as a servitor)
προσκαρτερέω.kj: attend (give self) continually (upon), continue (in, instant in, with), wait on (continually)
προσκαρτερέω.as:
προσ-καρτερέω, -ῶ
(< καρτερός, strong, stedfast), [in LXX: Nu 13:21 (חזק hith.), To 5:8א, Da Th Su 6*;]
to attend constantly, continue stedfastly, adhere to, wait on: c. dat. pers., Mk 3:9, Ac 8:1310:7; c. dat. rei, Ac 1:142:426:4, Ro 12:12, Col 4:2; seq. ἐν, Ac 2:46; εἰς, Ro 13:6.†

πρύμνα.as:
* πρύμνα, -ης, ἡ,
prop. fem. of adj. πρύμνος, -η, -ον, (sc. ναῦς), the hindmost part of a ship, the stern: Mk 4:38, Ac 27:29; opp. to πρῷρα, Ac 27:41.†

προσκεφάλαιον.sd: something for the head, i.e. a cushion
προσκεφάλαιον.der: neuter of a presumed compound of G4314 (πρός) and G2776 (κεφαλή);
προσκεφάλαιον.as:
προσ-κεφάλαιον, -ου, τό,
[in LXX: Ez 13:18, 20 (כֶּסֶת), I Es 3:8*;]
a pillow, cushion: Mk 4:38.†

πρασιά.long: a company formed into divisions (like garden-beds).
πρασιά.sd: a garden plot, i.e. (by implication, of regular beds) a row (repeated in plural by Hebraism, to indicate an arrangement)
πρασιά.der: perhaps from (a leek, and so an onion-patch);
πρασιά.as:
** πρασιά, -ᾶς, ἡ,
[in LXX: Si 24:31*;]
a garden-bed; metaph., of ranks or orderly groups of persons: Mk 6:40.†

προσορμίζομαι.sd: to moor to, i.e. (by implication) land at
προσορμίζομαι.der: from G4314 (πρός) and a derivative of the same as G3730 (ὁρμή) (meaning to tie (anchor) or lull);
προσορμίζομαι.as:
* προσ-ορμίζω
(< ὅρμος, an anchorage),
to bring a ship to anchor at; usually in mid., to come to anchor near, and so pass. in late writers (Ael., Dio Cass.): Mk 6:53.†

προστρέχω.sd: to run towards, i.e. hasten to meet or join
προστρέχω.der: from G4314 (πρός) and G5143 (τρέχω) (including its alternate);
προστρέχω.as:
προσ-τρέχω,
[in LXX for רוּץ;]
to run to: Mk 9:1510:17, Ac 8:30.†

προσκολλάομαι.long: (lit: I glue one thing to another), I join (unite) closely, cleave (to), follow as an adherent.
προσκολλάομαι.sd: to glue to, i.e. (figuratively) to adhere
προσκολλάομαι.as:
προσ-κολλάω, -ῶ,
[in LXX chiefly for דּבק;]
to glue to; pass., reflexive, to stick to, cleave to (Plat.): metaph. (c. dat., Jos 23:8, Si 6:34 al.), seq. πρός, Mk 10:7 (R, txt.), Eph 5:31(LXX).†

προσπορεύομαι.sd: to journey towards, i.e. approach (not the same as G4313 (προπορεύομαι))
προσπορεύομαι.as:
προσ-πορεύομαι,
[in LXX for קרב, נגשׁ, etc.;]
to come near, approach: c. dat. pers., Mk 10:35.†

πρόφασις.der: from a compound of G4253 (πρό) and G5316 (φαίνω);
πρόφασις.as:
πρό-φασις, -εως, ἡ
(< φήμι), [in LXX: Ps 140 (141):4 (עֲלִילָה), Da TH 6:4, 5 (5, 6) (עִלָּה), Pr 18:1, Ho 10:4*;]
a pretence, pretext: Mt 23:1 (WM, R, txt., om.), Mk 12:40, Lk 20:47, Jo 15:22, Ac 27:30, Phl 1:18, I Th 2:5.†

προμεριμνάω.long: I am anxious beforehand, ponder beforehand.

προλαμβάνω.g: I take before, anticipate, am overtaken
προλαμβάνω.long: I take before, anticipate; pass: I am caught or overtaken, taken by surprise.
προλαμβάνω.sd: to take in advance, i.e. (literally) eat before others have an opportunity; (figuratively) to anticipate, surprise
προλαμβάνω.as:
** προ-λαμβάνω,
[in LXX: Wi 17:11א2, Wi 17:17א2B*;]
1.to take beforehand: c. acc., I Co 11:21 (but v. infr.).
2.to be beforehand, anticipate (in cl., c. acc., gen. or dat.): c. inf. (= cl. φθάνω, v. Bl., § 69, 4; Swete, in l.), Mk 14:8.
3.to overtake, surprise: pass., Ga 6:1 (on the virtual disappearance of the temporal force of the preposition in this compound here and perhaps also in I Co 11:21, v. MM, xxi).†

προαύλιον.long: a porch, court before a building, vestibule.
προαύλιον.der: neuter of a presumed compound of G4253 (πρό) and G833 (αὐλή);
προαύλιον.as:
* προ-αύλιον, -ου, τό
(< πρό, αὐλή),
a porch, vestibule: Mk 14:68.†

προσάββατον.as:
† προ-σάββατον, -ου, τό,
[in LXX: Ps 91 (92) tit., א (שַׁבָּת) Ps 92 (93) tit., Jth 8:6*;]
the day before the Sabbath: Mk 15:42 (L, Tr., txt., πρὸς σ.).†

προσδέχομαι.long: (a) I await, expect, (b) I receive, welcome (originally: to my house), (c) I accept.
προσδέχομαι.sd: to admit (to intercourse, hospitality, credence, or (figuratively) endurance); by implication, to await (with confidence or patience)
προσδέχομαι.as:
προσ-δέχομαι,
[in LXX chiefly for רצה;]
1.to receive to oneself, receive favourably, admit, accept: c. acc. pers., Lk 15:2, Ro 16:2, Phl 2:29; c. acc. rei, Ac 24:15 (R, mg.), He 10:3411:35.
2.to expect, look for, wait for: c. acc. pers., Lk 12:36; c. acc. rei, Mk 15:43, Lk 2:25, 3823:51, Ac 23:21, Tit 2:13, Ju 21 (cf. δέχομαι).†

πρεσβύτης.as:
πρεσβύτης, -ου prose form of πρέσβυς, q.v.,
[in LXX chiefly for זָקֵן, Ge 25:8, al.; also (= πρεσβευτής), II Ch 32:31 B1 (מֵלִיץ), I Mac 14:22 S, al. (v. Thackeray, Gr., 97);]
1.an old man: Lk 1:18, Tit 2:2, Phm 9 (R, txt., but v. infr.).
2. As in LXX, also = πρεσβευτής, an ambassador: Phm 9 (R, mg., v. Lft. and ICC, in l.).†

προπορεύομαι.long: I precede, pass on before, go before.
προπορεύομαι.as:
προ-πορεύω,
[in LXX chiefly for הלךְ, also for עבר, etc.;]
to make to go before. Pass. and mid., to go before: Lk 1:76, Ac 7:40(LXX).†

πρωτότοκος.sd: first-born (usually as noun, literally or figuratively)
πρωτότοκος.der: from G4413 (πρῶτος) and the alternate of G5088 (τίκτω);
πρωτότοκος.as:
πρωτότοκος, -ον
(< πρῶτος, τίκτω), [in LXX chiefly for בְּכוֹר;]
first-born: Lk 2:7; pl., He 11:28. Metaph., of the priority of Christ (originally perh. a Messianic title, cf. Ps 88 (89):28, He 1:6; v. ICC on Col 1:15): He 1:6; π. πάσης κτίσεως, Col 1:15; ἐν πολλοῖς ἀδελφοῖς, Ro 8:29; π. (ἐκ) τ. νεκρῶν, Col 1:18, Re 1:5; pl., of the elect, ἐκκλησία πρωτοτόκων, He 12:23.†

προφῆτις.sd: a female foreteller or an inspired woman
προφῆτις.as:
προφῆτις, -ιδος, ἡ fem, of προφήτης,
[in LXX: Ex 15:20, Jg 4:4, IV Ki 22:14, II Ch 34:22, Is 8:3 (נְבִיאָה)*;]
a prophetess: Lk 2:36, Re 2:20.†

προκόπτω.long: (originally of the pioneer cutting his way through brushwood), I advance, progress, make progress.
προκόπτω.sd: to drive forward (as if by beating), i.e. (figuratively and intransitively) to advance (in amount, to grow; in time, to be well along)
προκόπτω.kj: increase, proceed, profit, be far spent, wax
προκόπτω.as:
** προ-κόπτω,
[in Sm.: Ps 44 (45):5*;]
to cut forward a way, forward, advance, in cl. trans. with neut. adj., as οὐδὲν π., τὰ πολλὰ π. In late writers (Polyb., al.), wholly intrans., to advance, progress: of time, Ro 13:12. Metaph., Lk 2:52, Ga 1:14, II Ti 2:163:9, 13.†

πράσσω.long: I do, perform, accomplish; be in any condition, i.e. I fare; I exact, require.
πράσσω.sd: to "practise", i.e. perform repeatedly or habitually (thus differing from G4160 (ποιέω), which properly refers to a single act); by implication, to execute, accomplish, etc.; specially, to collect (dues), fare (personally)
πράσσω.kj: commit, deeds, do, exact, keep, require, use arts
πράσσω.as:
πράσσω,
(Att. -ττω, and so Ac 17:7 Rec.; cf. M, Pr., 25, 45), [in LXX chiefly for עשׂה, פָּעַל;] = Lat agere, as ποιέω (q.v.) = facere,
1.to do, practise, be engaged in: Ac 19:19, 36, I Co 9:17; τ. ἴδια π., to mind one's own business (τὰ ἑαυτοῦ, Soph., Plat.), I Th 4:11; intrans., to act, Ac 17:7.
2.to achieve, effect, accomplish, perform: Ac 26:20, 26, Ro 7:159:11, II Co 5:10, Phl 4:9; νόμον (ICC, in l.), Ro 2:25; of unworthy acts (for wh. usually ποιέω in cl.), to commit, do: Lk 22:2323:41, Jo 3:205:29, Ac 3:175:3516:2825:11, 2526:9, 31, Ro 1:32 (ICC, in l.), 2:1-37:1913:4, I Co 5:2, II Co 12:21, Ga 5:21.
3.to transact, manage, hence, of payment, to exact (cl.): Lk 3:1319:23.
4. Reflexively, of state or condition, to do or fare (Æsch., Hdt., al.): Eph 6:21; εὖ π. (v. M, Pr., 228 f.), Ac 15:29.†
SYN.: v.s. ποιέω.

προδότης.der: from G4272 (προδίδωμι) (in the sense of giving forward into another's (the enemy's) hands);
προδότης.as:
** προ-δότης, -ου, ὁ
(προδίδωμι), [in LXX: II Mac 5:1510:13, 22, III Mac 3:24*;]
a betrayer, traitor: Lk 6:16, Ac 7:52, II Ti 3:4.†

προφέρω.as:
προ-φέρω,
[in LXX: Pr 10:13 (מצא ni.), To 9:5, al.;]
to bring forth: c. acc. rei, seq. ἐκ, Lk 6:45.†

προσρήγνυμι.sd: to tear towards, i.e. burst upon (as a tempest or flood)
προσρήγνυμι.as:
**† προσ-ρήγνυμι,
[in Aq.: Ps 2:9*;]
to break against, dash against;
(a) trans. (παιδία πέτραις, FlJ, Ant., ix, 4, 6);
(b) intrans., c. dat.: Lk 6:48, 49 (cf. προσπίπτω).†

προσαναλίσκω.as:
* προσ-αναλίσκω,
to spend besides: Lk 8:43 (WH, R, mg., om.).†

προσάγω.long: I bring to, bring near; I come to or towards, approach.
προσάγω.sd: to lead towards, i.e. (transitively) to conduct near (summon, present), or (intransitively) to approach
προσάγω.as:
προσ-άγω,
[in LXX chiefly for קרב hi., also for נגשׁ etc.;]
1. trans., to bring or lead: c. acc. et dat., Ac 16:20; metaph., τ. θεῷ, I Pe 3:18; seq. ὧδε, Lk 9:41; pass., c. dat., Mt 18:24 (προσηνέχθη, T); in forensic sense, to summon: Ac 12:6 (προαγαγεῖν, T, WH, mg., R).
2. Intrans., to draw near, approach (Jos 3:9, Je 26 (46):3, al.): c. dat., Ac 27:27 (WH, προσαχεῖν).†

προσδαπανάω.as:
*† προσ-δαπανάω, -ῶ,
to spend besides: c. acc., Lk 10:35.†
SYN.: προσαναλίσκω.

προσψαύω.sd: to impinge, i.e. lay a finger on (in order to relieve)
προσψαύω.as:
* προσ-ψαύω,
in poët. and late writers, to touch: c. dat., Lk 11:46.†

πράκτωρ.g: an officer employed to execute judicial sentences
πράκτωρ.long: an officer employed to execute judicial sentences.
πράκτωρ.sd: a practiser, i.e. (specially), an official collector
πράκτωρ.as:
πράκτωρ, -ορος, ὁ
(< πράσσω), [in LXX: Is 3:12 (נֹגֵשׂ)*;]
1. (poët.) one who does or accomplishes.
2. In Athens, one who exacts payment, a collector; hence, generally (freq. in π., v. Deiss., BS, 154), a court officer: Lk 12:58.†

προσαναβαίνω.g: I go up to, come up to
προσαναβαίνω.long: I go up to, come up to, go up further.
προσαναβαίνω.sd: to ascend farther, i.e. be promoted (take an upper (more honorable) seat)
προσαναβαίνω.as:
προσ-ανα-βαίνω,
[in LXX: Ex 19:23, al. (עלה);]
1.to go up besides.
2.to go up higher: Lk 14:10.†

πρεσβεία.sd: seniority (eldership), i.e. (by implication) an embassy (concretely, ambassadors)
πρεσβεία.as:
** πρεσβεία, -ας, ἡ
(< πρεσβεύω), [in LXX: II Mac 4:11*;]
1.age, seniority.
2.rank, dignity.
3.an embassy; by meton., of the ambassadors, embassy: Lk 14:3219:14.†

προτρέχω.long: I run before, outrun, run in advance.
προτρέχω.sd: to run forward, i.e. outstrip, precede
προτρέχω.der: from G4253 (πρό) and G5143 (τρέχω) (including its alternate);
προτρέχω.as:
προ-τρέχω,
[in LXX: I Ki 8:11 (לִפְנֵירוּץ), Jb 41:13 (14) A (דּוּץ), To 11:3 (seq. ἔμπροσθεν), I Mac 16:21*;]
1.to run forward.
2.to run on, run in advance: Jo 20:4; seq. εἰς τὸ ἔμπροσθεν, Lk 19:4.†

πραγματεύομαι.sd: to busy oneself with, i.e. to trade
πραγματεύομαι.as:
πραγματεύομαι
(< πρᾶγμα), [in LXX: III Ki 10:22 B, 9:19 A (חשׁק), Da LXX 8:27 (אֶת־מְלֶאכֶתעָשָׂה)*;]
1.to busy oneself.
2.to be engaged in business, esp. to trade: Lk 19:13 (cf. δια-πραγματεύομαι).†

προσεργάζομαι.sd: to work additionally, i.e. (by implication) acquire besides
προσεργάζομαι.as:
* προσ-εργάζομαι,
1.to work or do service besides (Hdt., Plut.).
2.to gain besides, by working or trading: Lk 19:16 (Xen.).†

προμελετάω.long: I meditate beforehand, prepare, get up, premeditate.

προσδοκία.sd: apprehension (of evil); by implication, infliction anticipated
προσδοκία.as:
προσδοκία, -ας, ἡ
(< προσδοκάω), [in LXX: Ge 49:10 (יִקְהָה), Ps 118 (119):116 (שֵׂבֶר), Wi 17:13, Si 40:2, al.;]
expectation: c. gen. obj., Lk 21:26; c. gen. subjc., Ac 12:11.†

προβάλλω.long: I thrust forward, put forth (as of branches), produce.
προβάλλω.sd: to throw forward, i.e. push to the front, germinate
προβάλλω.as:
προ-βάλλω,
[in LXX for חוּד, מרק, etc.;]
1.to throw before.
2.to put forward: c. acc., Ac 19:33; of trees, to put forth, produce (sc. φύλλα), Lk 21:30.†

πρεσβυτέριον.long: an assembly of elders, the Sanhedrin, officers of the church assembly, presbytery.
πρεσβυτέριον.sd: the order of elders, i.e. (specially), Israelite Sanhedrin or Christian "presbytery"
πρεσβυτέριον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of G4245 (πρεσβύτερος);
πρεσβυτέριον.as:
**† πρεσβυτέριον, -ου, τό
(< πρεσβύτερος), [in LXX: Da TH Su 50 A*;]
a body of elders, presbytery: of the Sanhedrin (cf. συνέδριον), Lk 22:66, Ac 22:5; of Christian presbyters, I Ti 4:14.†

προϋπάρχω.long: I have been already, have been previously.
προϋπάρχω.sd: to exist before, i.e. (adverbially) to be or do something previously
προϋπάρχω.as:
** προ-ϋπ-άρχω,
[in LXX: Jb 42:18*;]
1.to be beforehand in.
2.to be before or previously: c. ptcp., Lk 23:12, Ac 8:9.†

προσποιέομαι.long: I pretend, regard, make a show of.
προσποιέομαι.sd: to do forward for oneself, i.e. pretend (as if about to do a thing)
προσποιέομαι.der: middle voice from G4314 (πρός) and G4160 (ποιέω);
προσποιέομαι.as:
προσ-ποιέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: I Ki 21:13 (14) (הלל hithpo.), Jb 19:14, Si 34 (31):30, Da LXX Su 11*;]
to make over to, add or attach to. Mid., to take to oneself, claim; hence, to pretend; c. inf. (cf. Xen., Anab., iv, 3, 20), to make as if: Lk 24:28.†

προβατικός.sd: relating to sheep, i.e. (a gate) through which they were led into Jerusalem
προβατικός.as:
προβατικός, -ή, -όν
(< πρόβατον), [in LXX (π. πύλη): Ne 3:1, 3212:39 (צֹאן)*;]
of sheep: ἡ π. (sc. πύλη, v. supr.), the sheep-gate, Jo 5:2.†

πρότερος.as:
A. Compar., πρότερος, -α, -ον,
[in LXX for לִפָנִים, רִאשׁוֹן, etc.;]
before, of time, place, rank, etc.; in NT always of Time, before, former: Eph 4:22. Adverbially, πρότερον, before, aforetime, formerly: Jo 7:50, II Co 1:15, He 4:6; opp. to ἔπειτα, He 7:27; τὸ π., Jo 6:629:8, Ga 4:13, I Ti 1:13; αἱ π. ἡμέραι, He 10:32; αἱ π. ἐπιθυμίαι, I Pe 1:14.†

προσαιτέω.long: I beg, ask earnestly, ask for in addition.
προσαιτέω.as:
προσ-αιτέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: Jb 27:14*;]
1.to ask besides.
2.to continue asking; hence, to importune, beg, ask alms: Jo 9:8.†

προσφάγιον.long: anything eaten with bread, especially fish or meat.
προσφάγιον.sd: something eaten in addition to bread, i.e. a relish (specially, fish; compare G3795 (ὀψάριον))
προσφάγιον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of G4314 (πρός) and G5315 (φάγω);
προσφάγιον.as:
*† προσφάγιον, -ου, τό
(< φαγεῖν),
Hellenistic for ὄψον (v.s. ὀψάριον), a relish or dainty (esp. cooked fish), to be eaten with bread: Jo 21:5 (have ye taken any fish, Field, Notes, 109; Abbott, Essays, 105; cf. M, Pr., 170n; MM, Exp., xxi).†

πρηνής.as:
** πρηνής, -ές
(in Att. also πρανής), [in LXX: Wi 4:19, III Mac 5:43, 506:23*;]
headlong, prone: Ac 1:18.†

πρόγνωσις.as:
**† πρό-γνωσις, -εως, ἡ
(< προγινώσκω), [in LXX: Jth 9:611:19*;]
foreknowledge: Ac 2:23, I Pe 1:2.†

προσπήγνυμι.long: I fasten to, applied to Christ's being fastened to the cross.
προσπήγνυμι.sd: to fasten to, i.e. (specially), to impale (on a cross)

προοράω.long: I see beforehand, foresee, see previously, am mindful of; mid: I pay regard to, set before me.
προοράω.sd: to behold in advance, i.e. (actively) to notice (another) previously, or (middle voice) to keep in (one's own) view
προοράω.as:
προ-οράω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: Ps 15 (16):8) (שׁוה pi.), I Es 5:63 A*;]
to see before (as to place or time): c. acc., Ac 21:29. Mid., c. acc., seq. ἐνώπιόν μου, Ac 2:25(LXX).†

προκαταγγέλλω.sd: to anounce beforehand, i.e. predict, promise
προκαταγγέλλω.as:
*† προ-κατ-αγγέλλω,
to announce beforehand: c. acc. et inf., Ac 3:18; seq. περί, Ac 7:52.†

προχειρίζομαι.long: I appoint, choose, elect, take into hand.
προχειρίζομαι.sd: to handle for oneself in advance, i.e. (figuratively) to purpose
προχειρίζομαι.der: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and a derivative of G5495 (χείρ);
προχειρίζομαι.as:
προ-χειρίζω
(< πρόχειρος, at hand), [in LXX: Ex 4:13 (שׁלח), Jos 3:12 (לקח), Da LXX 3:22, II Mac 3:78:914:12 A*;]
1.to put into the hand, deliver up: pass., Ac 3:20.
2. More freq. as depon., -ομαι, to take into one's hand; hence, metaph., to propose, determine, choose: c. inf., Ac 22:14; c. acc. pers., Ac 26:16.†

προσαπειλέομαι.as:
** προσ-απειλέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: Si 13:3א*;]
to threaten further: Ac 4:21.†

προορίζω.long: I foreordain, predetermine, mark out beforehand.
προορίζω.sd: to limit in advance, i.e. (figuratively) predetermine
προορίζω.as:
*† προ-ορίζω,
to predetermine, foreordain: c. acc., Ro 8:30; id. et inf., Ac 4:28; id. seq. εἰς, I Co 2:7, Eph 1:5; c. dupl. acc., Ro 8:26; pass., Eph 1:11.†

προσκλίνομαι.as:
** προσ-κλίνω,
[in LXX: II Mac 14:24*;]
1.to make to lean against.
2.to make the scale incline one way or another; hence, metaph., of persons, to incline (sc. ἑαυτόν) towards: pass., Ac 5:36.†

Πρόχορος.long: Prochorus, one of the seven original deacons at Jerusalem.
Πρόχορος.sd: before the dance; Prochorus, a Christian

πρόσπεινος.der: from G4314 (πρός) and the same as G3983 (πεινάω);

προσωπολήμπτης.sd: an accepter of a face (individual), i.e. (specially), one exhibiting partiality
προσωπολήμπτης.as:
*† προσωπο-λήμπτης (Rec. -λήπτης, v. Bl., § 6, 8), -ου, ὁ
(< πρόσωπον λαμβάνειν, v.s. πρόσωπον),
a respecter of persons: Ac 10:34 (on this group of cognate forms, v. Mayor, ja., 78 f.; and cf. Thackeray, Gr., 44).†

προχειροτονέω.as:
* προ-χειρο-τονέω, -ῶ
(v. χειροτονέω),
to choose or appoint beforehand: Ac 10:41 (Plat., al.).†

προκηρύσσω.long: I announce or preach beforehand, announce by herald.
προκηρύσσω.as:
* προ-κηρύσσω,
1.to proclaim by herald.
2. Of one who acts as a herald, to proclaim: Ac 13:24.†

προσλαλέω.sd: to talk to, i.e. converse with
προσλαλέω.as:
προσ-λαλέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: Ex 4:16 AB2 (דּבר pi.), Wi 13:17*;]
to speak to: Ac 28:20; c. dat. pers., Ac 13:43.†

προπέμπω.long: I send forward, accompany, equip for a journey.
προπέμπω.sd: to send forward, i.e. escort or aid in travel
προπέμπω.kj: accompany, bring (forward) on journey (way), conduct forth
προπέμπω.as:
** προ-πέμπω,
[in LXX: I Es 4:47, Jth 10:15, Wi 19:2, I Mac 12:4, II Mac 6:23*;]
1.to send before, send forth.
2.to set forward on a journey, escort: c. acc. pers., I Co 16:11, Tit 3:13, III Jo 6; seq. εἰς, Ac 20:38; οὗ, I Co 16:6; ἕως, Ac 21:5; pass., Ac 15:3, Ro 15:24, II Co 1:16.†

προσκληρόομαι.long: I assign by lot, allot, associate with, follow as a disciple.
προσκληρόομαι.sd: to give a common lot to, i.e. (figuratively) to associate with
προσκληρόομαι.as:
*† προσ-κληρόω, -ῶ,
to allot to, assign to by lot; pass. (but perh. as mid., EV, consorted with, so Syr.): Ac 17:4 (for exx., v, Cremer, 749).†

προθυμία.kj: forwardness of mind, readiness (of mind), ready (willing) mind
προθυμία.as:
** προθυμία, -ας, ἡ
(< πρόθυμος), [in LXX: Si 45:23*;]
eagerness, willingness, readiness: Ac 17:11, II Co 8:11, 12, 199:2.†

προσδέομαι.long: I want more, need in addition.
προσδέομαι.sd: to require additionally, i.e. want further
προσδέομαι.as:
προσ-δέομαι,
[in LXX: Pr 12:9חָסֵר, Si6*;]
to want further, need in addition: Ac 17:25.†

προσφάτως.as:
προσφάτως,
adv.
(v.s. πρόσφατος), [in LXX: De 24:5 (חָדָשׁ), Jth 4:3, 5, Ez 11:3, II Mac 14:36*;]
recently: Ac 18:2 (v. MM, Exp., xxi).†

Πρίσκιλλα.long: Prisca, Priscilla, the former being the more correct and formal name, the latter a diminutive and more familiar; a Roman lady, probably of good birth, wife of the Jewish Christian Aquila.
Πρίσκιλλα.sd: Priscilla (i.e. little Prisca), a Christian woman

προτρέπομαι.sd: to turn forward for oneself, i.e. encourage
προτρέπομαι.der: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and the base of G5157 (τροπή);
προτρέπομαι.as:
** προ-τρέπω,
[in LXX: Wi 14:18, II Mac 11:7, IV Mac 12:715:1216:13*;]
to urge forwards, exhort, persuade. Mid., in same sense (as also in cl.): Ac 18:27.†

προπετής.der: from a compound of G4253 (πρό) and G4098 (πίπτω);
προπετής.as:
προπετής, -ές
(< προπίπτω), [in LXX: Pr 10:14 (אֱוִיל) 13:3 (פֹּשׂק) Si 9:18*;]
falling forwards, headlong. Metaph., precipitate, rash, reckless: of persons, II Ti 3:4; of things, Ac 19:36.†

προσφορά.sd: presentation; concretely, an oblation (bloodless) or sacrifice
προσφορά.as:
προσ-φορά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(< προσφέρω), [in LXX: III Ki 7:48 (פָּנִים) Ps 39 (40):6 (מִנְחָה), I Es 5:52, Si 14:11, al.;]
1.a bringing to, offering (Plat., al.).
2. (Less freq. in cl.), a present, an offering; in NT, of sacrificial offerings: Ac 21:2624:17, Eph 5:2, He 10:5, 8, 14; περί ἁμαρτίας, He 10:18; c. gen. obj., Ro 15:16, He 10:10.†

προτείνω.long: I stretch out, tie up (for scourging), extend before.
προτείνω.sd: to protend, i.e. tie prostrate (for scourging)
προτείνω.as:
** προ-τείνω, [in LXX: II Mac7, III Mac 2:1*;]
to stretch out, stretch forth: of preparations for scourging (v. Field, Notes, 136 f.), Ac 22:25.†

πρόνοια.sd: forethought, i.e. provident care or supply
πρόνοια.as:
πρόνοια, -ας, ἡ
(< πρόνοος, careful), [in LXX: Da LXX 6:18 (19) Wi 14:317:2, II-IV Mac6*;]
foresight, forethought: Ac 24:3; π. ποιεῖσθαι, c. gen. (Dem., 546, 6), make provision for, show care for: Ro 13:14.†

πρωτοστάτης.long: one who stands in the front rank, hence: a leader, ringleader, chief.
πρωτοστάτης.sd: one standing first in the ranks, i.e. a captain (champion)
πρωτοστάτης.as:
πρωτοστάτης, -ου, ὁ
(< πρῶτος, ἵστημι), [in LXX: Jb 15:24 AB*;]
prop., of soldiers, one who stands first, one in the front rank (Thuc., Xen.); hence, metaph., a leader: Ac 24:5.†

προγινώσκω.as:
** προ-γινώσκω,
[in LXX: Wi 6:138:818:6*;]
to know beforehand, foreknow: II Pe 3:17; c. acc. pers., Ac 26:5; of the Divine foreknowledge, Ro 8:2911:2, I Pe 1:20.†

προσεάω.long: I permit one to approach, permit further.

πρῷρα.sd: the prow, i.e. forward part of a vessel
πρῷρα.der: feminine of a presumed derivative of G4253 (πρό) as noun;
πρῷρα.as:
* πρῷρα (Rec. incorrectly πρώρα, v. Bl., § 3, 3; LS, s.v.), -ης (for Att. -ας, v. Bl., § 7, 1; Mayser, l 2), ἡ,
the forward part of a ship, the prow: Ac 27:30; opp. to πρύμνα, Ac 27:41.†

προεπαγγέλλομαι.der: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G1861 (ἐπαγγέλλω);
προεπαγγέλλομαι.as:
*† προ-επ-αγγέλλω,
to announce before. Mid., to promise before: c. acc. rei, Ro 1:2, II Co 9:5 (Dio. Cass.).†

προτίθεμαι.sd: to place before, i.e. (for oneself) to exhibit; (to oneself) to propose (determine)
προτίθεμαι.der: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G5087 (τίθημι);
προτίθεμαι.as:
προ-τίθημι,
[in LXX: Ex 40:4, 23, Le 24:8 (ערךְ) Ps 53 (54):3 (שׂוּם), etc.;]
1.to set before, set forth publicly; so also in mid.: c. acc. pers., Ro 3:25 (for a suggested alt. rend., v. MM, xxii).
2. Mid., to set before oneself, propose, purpose: c. inf., Ro 1:13; c. acc. rei, Eph 1:9.†

προσωπολημψία.as:
*† προσωπολημψία (Rec. -ληψία), -ας, ἡ
(< προσωπολήμπτης),
respect of persons: Ro 2:11, Eph 6:9, Col 3:25, Ja 2:1 (v. Mayor, in l.).†

προέχομαι.long: trans: I hold before; mid: I excuse myself; intrans: I project, excel, surpass, have preeminence.
προέχομαι.sd: to hold oneself before others, i.e. (figuratively) to excel
προέχομαι.der: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G2192 (ἔχω);
προέχομαι.as:
προ-έχω,
[in LXX: Jb 27:6 A (חזק hi.)*;]
1. Trans., to hold before; mid., to hold something before oneself (Hdt.), hence, metaph., to excuse oneself: Ro 3:9, R, mg. (but v. Field, Notes, 152 f.; Lft., Notes, 266 f.; ICC and Vau., in l.).
2. Intrans.
(a)to project;
(b) in running, to have the start, hence, metaph., to excel: pass., Ro 3:9, R, txt. (v. reff. supr.).†

προαιτιάομαι.sd: to accuse already, i.e. previously charge
προαιτιάομαι.der: from G4253 (πρό) and a derivative of G156 (αἰτία);
προαιτιάομαι.as:
*† προ-αιτιάομαι, -ῶμαι,
to accuse or charge beforehand: Ro 3:9 (not elsewhere).†

προγίνομαι.sd: to be already, i.e. have previousy transpired
προγίνομαι.as:
** προ-γίνομαι,
[in LXX: Wi 19:13אA, II Mac 14:315:8*;]
to happen before: pf. pass. ptcp., Ro 3:25.†

προπάτωρ.as:
** προ-πάτωρ, -ορος, ὁ
(< πατήρ), [in LXX: III Mac 2:21 A*;]
a forefather: Ro 4:1.†

προσαγωγή.as:
* προσ-αγωγή, -ῆς, ἡ,
(< προσάγω),
1.a bringing to.
2.approach, access (v. Lft., Notes, 284; MM, xxi): Ro 5:2, Eph 2:183:12 (but v. Ellic., Eph., 59 f., where the transitive sense "introduction" is advocated).†

προετοιμάζω.long: I prepare or appoint beforehand, predestine.
προετοιμάζω.sd: to fit up in advance (literally or figuratively)
προετοιμάζω.as:
προ-ετοιμάζω,
[in LXX: Is 28:24 B, Wi 9:8*;]
to prepare before: c. acc. rei, Ro 9:23 (οἷς for ἅ by attraction), Eph 2:10.†

πρόσκομμα.long: a stumbling-block, an occasion for falling, a moral embarrassment.
πρόσκομμα.sd: a stub, i.e. (figuratively) occasion of apostasy
πρόσκομμα.as:
† πρόσ-κομμα, -τος, τό
(< προσκόπτω), [in LXX: Ex 23:3334:12 (מוֹקֵשׁ), Is 8:14 (נֶגֶף), Jth 8:22, Si 17:25, al.;]
(a)a stumble, stumbling: λίθος προσκόμματος (= אֶבֶןנֶגֶף, Is 8:14), fig., Ro 9:32, 33, I Pe 2:8(LXX);
(b) = προσκοπή, an occasion of stumbling, a stumbling-block: metaph., Ro 14:13, 20, I Co 8:9 (Plut.).†
SYN.: σκάνδαλον (cf. Cremer, 752 f.).

πρόσλημψις.long: a receiving, a taking to one's self, acceptance.
πρόσλημψις.as:
* πρόσ-λημψις (Rec. -ληψις, as in Att.), -εως, ἡ
(< προσλαμβάνω),
1.an assumption (Plat.).
2.a receiving (cf. προσλαμβάνω): Ro 11:15.†

προδίδωμι.long: I give before, give forth, betray.
προδίδωμι.sd: to give before the other party has given
προδίδωμι.as:
προ-δίδωμι,
[in LXX: Ez 16:34 A (נתן), IV Mac 4:1, al.;]
1.to give before, give first: Ro 11:35 (Jb 41:2 (11) LXX, al.).
2.to betray (IV Mac 4:1).†

προΐστημι.long: I preside, rule over, give attention to, direct, maintain, practice diligently.
προΐστημι.sd: to stand before, i.e. (in rank) to preside, or (by implication) to practise
προΐστημι.as:
προ-ΐστημι,
[in LXX: II Ki 13:17, Pr 23:526:17, Is 43:24, Am 6:10 (no proper Heb. equiv.), Da LXX Bel 7, I Mac 5:19, IV Mac 11:27*;]
1. trans. in fut., 1 aor., and mid. 1 aor., to put before, set over (Plat., al.).
2. Intrans., in pf., plpf., 2 aor. and mid. pres. and impf.;
(a)to preside, rule, govern: Ro 12:8, I Ti 5:17; c. gen., I Th 5:12, I Ti 3:4, 5, 12;
(b)to direct, maintain: c. gen. rei, καλῶν ἔργων, Tit 3:8, 14 (on R, mg., profess honest occupations, v. CGT, in l.; Field, Notes, 223 f.).†

προηγέομαι.long: I lead onward by example, go before, prefer.
προηγέομαι.sd: to lead the way for others, i.e. show deference
προηγέομαι.as:
προ-ηγέομαι,
[in LXX: De 20:9 (בְּרוֹשׁ), Pr 17:14 (לִפְנֵי), II Mac 4:40, al.;]
1.to go before as leader (in cl., c. gen., dat.): Ro 12:10 (Chrys., Vg., al.; v. ICC, in l.).
2. In a sense not elsewhere found, ἀλλήλους προηγούμενοι = ἀ. ἡγούμενοι ὑπερέχοντας: Ro 12:10 (ICC, cf. I Th 5:13, Phl 2:3 and EV "preferring").†

προνοέω.long: I take thought for beforehand, provide for, practice.
προνοέω.sd: to consider in advance, i.e. look out for beforehand (actively, by way of maintenance for others; middle voice by way of circumspection for oneself)
προνοέω.as:
προ-νοέω, -ῶ, and depon. -έομαι, οῦμαι,
[in LXX: Da LXX 11:37 (בִּין), Wi 6:7, al.;]
1.to foresee.
2.to provide (RV, take thought for): c. acc. rei, καλά, Ro 12:17 (-ούμενοι), II Co 8:21 (-οῦμεν).
3.to provide for (seq. περί, Wi 6:7): c. gen. pers., I Ti 5:8 (-εῖ, WH, mg., -εῖται).†

προγράφω.long: (a) I write previously (aforetime); I write above (already), (b) I depict or portray openly, (c) I designate beforehand.
προγράφω.sd: to write previously; figuratively, to announce, prescribe
προγράφω.kj: before ordain, evidently set forth, write (afore, aforetime)
προγράφω.as:
προ-γράφω,
[in LXX: Da LXX 3:3cod., I Mac 10:36*;]
1.to write before: Ro 15:4, Eph 3:3, Ju 4.
2.to write in public, placard, proclaim (Dem., Plut., al.): Ga 3:1 (Lft., in l.).
3. = ζωγραφέω, to pourtray, depict: Ga 3:1 (Syr. Pesh., Chrys.; Field, Notes, 189; CGT, in l.).†

προστάτις.der: feminine of a derivative of G4291 (προΐστημι);
προστάτις.as:
* προστάτις, -ιδος, ἡ
(fem. of προστάτης),
a patroness, protectress: Ro 16:2.†

Πρίσκα.long: Prisca, Priscilla, the former being the more correct and formal name, the latter a diminutive and more familiar; a Roman lady, probably of good birth, wife of the Jewish Christian Aquila.
Πρίσκα.sd: feminine of Priscus, ancient; Priska, a Christian woman
Πρίσκα.as:
Πρίσκα, -ας, ἡ (Lat.), and Πρίσκιλλα, -ης, ἡ,
Prisca: Ro 16:3, I Co 16:19, II Ti 4:19; Priscilla: Ac 18:2, 18, 26; the wife of Aquila, v.s. Ἀκύλας.†

πραΰτης.as:
πραΰτης
(Rec. -ότης, exc. Ja 1:213:13, I Pe 3:15, where πρᾳύτης), -ητος, ἡ, late form of πραότης, [in LXX: Ps 44 (45):489 (90):10131 (132):1 (עַנְוָה, עֻנּוֹת, Es 5:1, Si6*;]
gentleness, meekness: I Co 4:21, II Co 10:1, Ga 5:236:1, Eph 4:2, Col 3:12 (v. Lft., in l.), II Ti 2:25, Tit 3:2, Ja 1:213:13, I Pe 3:15.†
SYN.: ἐπιεικία, q.v.

πρεσβεύω.g: I am aged, act as an ambassador
πρεσβεύω.long: I am aged, act as an ambassador.
πρεσβεύω.sd: to be a senior, i.e. (by implication) act as a representative (figuratively, preacher)
πρεσβεύω.as:
* πρεσβεύω
(< πρέσβυς),
1.to be the elder, to take precedence.
2.to be an ambassador (v.s. πρεσβύτης): II Co 5:20, Eph 6:20.†

προσκοπή.long: a cause of stumbling, offense, shock.
προσκοπή.sd: a stumbling, i.e. (figuratively and concretely) occasion of sin
προσκοπή.as:
** προσκοπή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< προσκόπτω), [in Gr. Ven.: Pr 16:18 (כִּשָּׁלוֹן)*;]
an occasion of stumbling, offence: II Co 6:3.†

προενάρχομαι.as:
*† προ-ενάρχομαι,
to begin before: II Co 8:6; c. acc., τὸ θέλειν, II Co 8:10 (not elsewhere).†

πρόκειμαι.long: I am set (placed, put) before, am already there.
πρόκειμαι.sd: to lie before the view, i.e. (figuratively) to be present (to the mind), to stand forth (as an example or reward)
πρόκειμαι.as:
πρό-κειμαι,
[in LXX: Ex 39:18 (36), Nu 4:7 (פָּנִים), etc.;] used as pass. of προτίθημι;
1.to be set before one, to be set forth: He 6:1812:1, 2, Ju 7.
2.to present oneself, be present: II Co 8:12 (v. Mey., in l.).†

προαιρέομαι.long: I propose; mid: I propose to myself, purpose.
προαιρέομαι.sd: to choose for oneself before another thing (prefer), i.e. (by implication) to propose (intend)
προαιρέομαι.as:
προ-αιρέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: for חשׁק, etc.;]
to bring forth or forward. Most freq. in mid., to take by choice, prefer, propose: II Co 9:7.†

προσαναπληρόω.long: I fill up by adding to, supply.
προσαναπληρόω.sd: to fill up further, i.e. furnish fully
προσαναπληρόω.as:
** προσ-αναπληρόω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: Wi 19:4*;]
to fill up by adding to, to supply fully: II Co 9:1211:9.†

προσανατίθημι.sd: to lay up in addition, i.e. (middle voice and figuratively) to impart or (by implication) to consult
προσανατίθημι.as:
* προσ-ανα-τίθημι,
to lay on or offer besides; mid.,
(a)to lay on oneself in addition, undertake besides;
(b) c. gen. pers., of giving or obtaining information, to consult, communicate: Ga 1:162:6 (Lft., in l.; cf. ἀνα-τίθημι).

προευαγγελίζομαι.long: I preach the gospel beforehand, foretell good tidings.
προευαγγελίζομαι.sd: to announce glad news in advance
προευαγγελίζομαι.der: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G2097 (εὐαγγελίζω);

προκαλέομαι.long: I provoke, stimulate, challenge, call out.
προκαλέομαι.sd: to call forth to oneself (challenge), i.e. (by implication) to irritate
προκαλέομαι.der: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G2564 (καλέω);
προκαλέομαι.as:
** προ-καλέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: II Mac 8:11 A*;]
to call forth. Most freq. in mid.,
(a)to challenge; hence, to provoke: Ga 5:26;
(b)to invite (II Mac 8:11).†

προελπίζω.long: I hope before, am the first to hope.
προελπίζω.sd: to hope in advance of other confirmation

προκοπή.as:
**† προ-κοπή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< προκόπτω), [in LXX: Si 51:17, II Mac 8:8*;]
progress (prop., on a journey, then generally): Phl 1:12, 25, I Ti 4:15 (condemned by Atticists, v. Rutherford, NPhr., 158).†

προσφιλής.der: from a presumed compound of G4314 (πρός) and G5368 (φιλέω);
προσφιλής.as:
** προσφιλής, -ές
(< φιλέω), [in LXX: Es 5:1, Si 4:720:13*;]
(a) of persons, in both act. and pass. sense (LXX, Es 5:1, Si 4:720:13);
(b) of things, pleasing, agreeable (EV, lovely): Phl 4:8.†

προακούω.as:
* προ-ακούω,
to hear beforehand: Col 1:5 (v. Lft., in l.).†

πρωτεύω.long: I have preeminence, am chief, am first.
πρωτεύω.sd: to be first (in rank or influence)
πρωτεύω.as:
πρωτεύω
(< πρῶτος), [in LXX: Es 5:11, II Mac 6:1813:15*;]
to be first, pre-eminent, have the first place: Col 1:18.†

προσηλόω.long: I fasten with nails, nail to.
προσηλόω.sd: to peg to, i.e. spike fast
προσηλόω.der: from G4314 (πρός) and a derivative of G2247 (ἧλος);
προσηλόω.as:
** προσ-ηλόω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: III Mac 4:9*;]
to nail to: c. acc. et dat., fig., Col 2:14.†

πρῶτον.long: first, in the first place, before, formerly.
πρῶτον.sd: firstly (in time, place, order, or importance)
πρῶτον.kj: before, at the beginning, chiefly (at, at the) first (of all)
πρῶτον.der: neuter of G4413 (πρῶτος) as adverb (with or without G3588 (ὁ));

πρόγονος.as:
** πρό-γονος, -ον
(< προγίνομαι), [in LXX: Es 4:17, Si 8:4, al.;]
1.born before.
2. As subst., in pl., οἱ π., ancestors, forefathers: II Ti 1:3; of living parents (so Plat.), I Ti 5:4.†

πρόκριμα.der: from a compound of G4253 (πρό) and G2919 (κρίνω);
πρόκριμα.as:
*† πρό-κριμα, -τος, τό
(< cl. προκρίνειν, 1. to prefer. 2. to judge beforehand),
pre-judging, prejudice: I Ti 5:21 (v. Cremer, 378).†

πρόσκλισις.der: from a compound of G4314 (πρός) and G2827 (κλίνω);

πρόδηλος.long: manifest to all, evident, very clear.
πρόδηλος.sd: plain before all men, i.e. obvious
πρόδηλος.as:
** πρό-δηλος, -ον,
[in LXX: Jth 8:29, II Mac 3:1714:39*;]
1.evident beforehand.
2.clearly evident: I Ti 5:24, 25, He 7:14.†

πραϋπαθία.as:
*† πραϋπαθία (Rec. -πάθεια), -ας, ἡ
(< πραΰς, πάσχω), = πραΰτης,
meekness, gentleness: I Ti 6:11 (Philo.).†

πραγματεία.long: a business, an occupation, affair, transaction.

πρεσβῦτις.as:
** πρεσβῦτις, -ιδος, ἡ, fem, of πρεσβύτης,
[in LXX: IV Mac 16:14*;]
an aged woman: Tit 2:3.†

προσοχθίζω.long: I am displeased or offended with.
προσοχθίζω.der: from G4314 (πρός) and a form of (to be vexed with something irksome);
προσοχθίζω.as:
† προσ-οχθίζω,
[in LXX: Le 26:15, al. (גּעל); Le 18:25, al. (קוֹא), Ps 94 (95):10, Ez 36:31 (קוּט), Si 6:25, al. (other writers use ὀχθέω, rarely -ίζω);]
to be angry with: c. dat., He 3:10(LXX), 17.†

προσαγορεύω.long: I address by name, designate, accost.
προσαγορεύω.sd: to address, i.e. salute by name
προσαγορεύω.der: from G4314 (πρός) and a derivative of G58 (ἀγορά) (mean to harangue);
προσαγορεύω.as:
προσ-αγορεύω,
[in LXX: De 23:6 (7) (דָּרַשׁ), II Es 10:11, B:1 (ידה hith.), Wi 14:22, I Mac 14:40, II Mac 1:364:710:914:37*;]
to address, greet, salute; hence, to call by name, address, style: c. dupl. acc., pass., He 5:10.†

πρόδρομος.sd: a runner ahead, i.e. scout (figuratively, precursor)
πρόδρομος.as:
πρό-δρομος, -ον
(< προτρέχω), [in LXX: Nu 13:21 (20), Is 28:4 (בּכר), Wi 12:8*;]
running forward, going in advance. As subst., ὁ π., an advance guard, forerunner: He 6:20.†

πρόσφατος.long: (originally: newly slaughtered, freshly killed), recent, new.
πρόσφατος.der: from G4253 (πρό) and a derivative of G4969 (σφάζω);
πρόσφατος.as:
πρόσφατος, -ον
(on the derivation, v. Boisacq, s.v. and cf. -ως), [in LXX: Nu 6:3 (לַח), De 32:17, Ec 1:9 (חָדָשׁ), Ps 80 (81):9 (זוּר), Si 9:10*;]
1. originally, freshly slain.
2. Generally (from Æsch. on), new, fresh, recent: ὁδός, He 10:20 (v. MM, Exp., xxi; Rutherford, NPhr., 471 f.).†

πρόσχυσις.long: a pouring upon, an effusion, a sprinkling.
πρόσχυσις.der: from a comparative of G4314 (πρός) and (to pour);
πρόσχυσις.as:
*† πρόσ-χυσις, -εως, ἡ,
a pouring or sprinkling upon: He 11:28.†

πρίζω.der: a strengthened form of a primary prio (to saw);
πρίζω.as:
πρίζω = πρίω,
[in LXX: Am 1:3, Da TH Su 59*;]
to saw, saw asunder (= π. δίχα, Thuc., iv, 100): pass, He 11:37 (cf. δια-πρίω).†

προβλέπομαι.sd: to look out beforehand, i.e. furnish in advance
προβλέπομαι.as:
† προ-βλέπω,
[in LXX: Ps 36 (37):13 (ראה)*;]
to foresee: mid., He 11:40 (v. Bl., § 24, 55, 1).†

πρωτοτόκια.long: the birthright, the rights of the first-born.
πρωτοτόκια.as:
† πρωτοτόκια, -ων, τά
(< πρωτότοκος), [in LXX (with v.l. -εῖα, -εία): Ge 25:31 ff. 27:36, De 21:17, I Ch 5:1 (בְּכוֹרָה)*;]
the rights of the first-born, birthright (= cl. ἡ πρεσβεία): He 12:16.†

προσωπολημπτέω.sd: to favor an individual, i.e. show partiality
προσωπολημπτέω.as:
*† προσωπολημπτέω (Rec. -ληπτ-), -ῶ
(< -λήμπτης, q.v.),
to have respect of persons: Ja 2:9.†

πρόϊμος.as:
πρόϊμος (Rec. πρώ-, of which προ- is a late form; v. Bl., § 6, 4; WH, App., 152), -ον,
[in LXX: De 11:14 (יוֹרֶה), etc.;] = the more common πρώιος (q.v.),
early: of rain (as most freq. in LXX), Ja 5:7.†

προμαρτύρομαι.long: I predict, testify or protest beforehand.
προμαρτύρομαι.sd: to be a witness in advance i.e. predict
προμαρτύρομαι.as:
*† προ-μαρτύρομαι,
to protest beforehand (cf. μαρτύρομαι, and V. Hort, in l.): I Pe 1:11 (elsewhere only in Theod. Met., xiv/AD.).†

προθύμως.long: readily, eagerly, with a ready mind, cheerfully.
προθύμως.as:
προθύμως,
[in LXX: II Ch 29:34 (לֵבָביִשְׁרֵי), To 7:8, al.;]
eagerly, readily, with a ready mind: I Pe 5:2.†

προφητικός.as:
*† προφητικός, -ά, -όν
(< προφήτης),
of prophecy, prophetic: Ro 16:26, II Pe 1:19.†

πρωϊνός.sd: pertaining to the dawn, i.e. matutinal
πρωϊνός.as:
† πρωινός
(Rec. -ϊνος, v. WH, App., ή, -όν (< πρωί), [in LXX chiefly for בֹּקֶר;] = cl. πρώιος,
at early morn, early: ἀστήρ, Re 2:2822:16.†
